page: Microsoft Azure M64ls is a memory-optimized virtual machine from the MS family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 64 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 32 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8280M processor operating at 2.7 GHz. The x86_64 architecture supports hyper-threading and features 38 MB of L3 cache. It is equipped with 512 GB of RAM, providing 8 GB of memory per core, alongside 2097 GB of local storage with Premium Storage capabilities.

Benchmark data reveals a clear performance profile. Single-core performance is relatively weak, with stress-ng and Geekbench single-core scores falling into the bottom 10%. However, the server demonstrates robust multi-threaded capabilities, achieving average to strong results in multi-core processing and bzip3 multi-threaded decompression. Memory performance is a key strength, particularly in large-block read-only operations where it ranks in the top 25% of tested systems, though large-block write speeds remain average.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the M64ls offers high resource density for memory-bound workloads, though the lower single-core performance represents a tradeoff for single-threaded tasks. It is highly suited for large-scale databases, memory-intensive enterprise applications, multi-threaded data processing, and static web serving. It is less optimal for workloads requiring high single-core throughput or real-time LLM text generation.
description: Microsoft Azure M64ls is an x86_64 memory-optimized virtual machine powered by an Intel Xeon 8280M processor with 64 dedicated vCPUs and 32 physical cores. It features 512 GB of RAM and 2097 GB of Premium Storage-capable local storage. Operating on Microsoft Hyper-V, the instance exhibits a distinct performance profile characterized by lower single-core processing speeds but strong multi-threaded capabilities and high memory bandwidth, particularly in large-block read-only operations. Qualitatively, the server provides high memory density, making it a cost-effective choice for memory-intensive workloads despite the single-core performance tradeoff. It is best suited for large-scale databases, enterprise applications, and multi-threaded data processing tasks.
